Consider all circular sectors $MON$ with area $A=100$ square units. Determine the angle $\theta $ (in radians) of the circular sector that has the smallest possible perimeter. Do not round the answer.

$\theta =$
{{field-1}}  radians
question.worked_solution:
We let $r$ be the radius of the circular sector and let $\theta $ be the angle (in radians) subtended by it. Then, we want to minimize the perimeter

$$
P=2r+r\theta .
$$

We know that the area is fixed at $100$ square units, so we also have the constraint condition

$$
100=\frac{1}{2}{r}^{2}\theta .
$$

Now, by making $\theta $ the subject of the constraint equation and taking into account that $r>0,$ we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}100 & =\frac{1}{2}{r}^{2}\theta  \\ \theta  & =\frac{200}{{r}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging this into our expression for $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =2r+r\theta  \\  & =2r+r\cdot \frac{200}{{r}^{2}} \\  & =2r+\frac{200}{r}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to minimize $P,$ so we need to differentiate $P$ and set the derivative equal to zero. Computing the derivative gives 

$$
{P}^{′}(r)=2-\frac{200}{{r}^{2}}.
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2-\frac{200}{{r}^{2}} & =0 \\ 2{r}^{2} & =200 \\ {r}^{2} & =100 \\ r & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we confirm that $r=10$ is a minimum using the second derivative test.

Since the second derivative ${P}^{″}(r)=\frac{400}{{r}^{3}}>0,$ the stationary point $r=10$ is a minimum. 

Finally, when $r=10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\frac{200}{{r}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{200}{100} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
